title: Fylgja platform package 1
description: What Fylgja must know of one network operating system that the runtime's kind does not already know. Written as YAML (packages/<id>.yaml), read by the compiler, the drivers' plan, the push, readiness, verify and the conformance suite.
$comment: PLATFORM-LEVEL sections (id, versions, interfaces, push, readiness, gnmi, conformance, fidelity) are shared by every driver; what differs by runtime lives under runtime.<runtime>, and only runtime.containerlab exists now (both containerlab drivers read it; runtime.hardware arrives with that driver). A package states nothing a kind already provides: interface aliases, default logins and default configuration are the kind's. CROSS-FIELD RULES the core holds when it loads a package (POST /v1/packages:validate reports all of them in one pass): interface rule names unique (package.rule.name); exactly one management rule (package.management.rule); a template uses only placeholders its match captures (package.patterns.placeholders); every runtime.containerlab.rename entry names a data rule, and every data rule has one when alias is false (package.rename.coverage); a ranges key is a placeholder of match (package.ranges.placeholder). FIXED, not fields: the push is a replace with an explicit commit, the startup format is cli, the scheme is https, the gNMI encoding is json_ietf, and readiness is an authenticated request to the push transport. LOSSINESS is never declared: the driver's plan computes it from the rename rules.

platform_package_version.description: The format's version; the package loader refuses any other (rule package.version.unsupported).

id.description: The platform's identity; a blueprint device's platform names it, the compiler loads by it, and the bundle's nodes and mapping record it.

versions.description: Software versions the package was measured on, as prefixes; the conformance suite checks a booted node's version leaf against them.

credentials.description: The name the credential provider resolves to this platform's node login (environment locally, a Secret on a cluster); the push, readiness, verify and the conformance suite ask the provider for it. Never a value.

rules.description: Ordered; the first rule whose match fits a production name decides it. The compiler uses them to decide which names the platform has (in range, out of range, no rule) and each port's node name.

interfaces.description: How production interface names relate to the platform's ports; read by the compiler and by the driver's plan through rule names.

delivery.description: The push mechanism (SR Linux JSON-RPC cli, EOS eAPI runCmds in a configuration session); the push selects its client by it. Always a replace with an explicit, atomic commit.

port.description: The HTTPS port the push and readiness dial at the node's management address.

timeout_s.description: Measured bound on one push request; the push gives up and records push.timeout after it.

push.description: How the configuration reaches a booted node; read by the push and by readiness.

timeout_s.description: Measured bound, from apply's end, on the push transport answering an authenticated request; the reconcile loop's ready phase fails with readiness.timeout after it.

readiness.description: A node is ready when its push transport answers; read by the reconcile loop's ready phase.

port.description: The gNMI port verify and the conformance suite dial at the node's management address.

tls.description: Whether verify and the conformance suite dial gNMI over TLS (the boot-time certificate accepted unverified) or plaintext.

gnmi.description: How a node's state is read; encoding is always json_ietf.

host_name.description: The leaf holding the node's host name; verify asserts it equals the node's name.

version.description: The leaf holding the software version; the conformance suite matches it against versions.

enabled.description: The leaf and value saying a port is admin-enabled; verify asserts it on each enabled cabled port.

discovering.description: The leaf and value saying LLDP runs on a port; verify asserts it before reading neighbours.

path.description: The list of a port's LLDP neighbours; verify reads it to check each link's far end.

system_name.description: The far node's host name, relative to a neighbour entry; verify compares it with the link's far node.

port_id.description: The far port as the far node names it, relative to a neighbour entry; verify compares it with the far port's node name.

neighbor.description: Where verify reads a port's neighbour.

port.description: Per-port reads; {node_name} renders the port's node name.

conformance.description: The gNMI paths verify and the conformance suite read on a booted node.

approximations.description: How a twin of this platform differs from production, asserted; the compile result's and each deployment's fidelity list them.

fidelity.description: What the package asserts about its own fidelity; forwarding is the deployment's.

containerlab.description: The section the local containerlab driver and the clabernetes driver both read.

runtime.description: Per-runtime sections, each read only by that runtime's drivers' plan and admission.

pattern.description: A naming template: {name} captures one path segment ([^/]+), everything else is literal.

path.description: An absolute gNMI path; {node_name} renders a port's node name.

value.description: What the leaf must read for verify's assertion to hold.

absent.description: The value verify takes an unreported leaf to mean (cEOS reports nothing while LLDP runs); without it nothing read fails.

range.description: Inclusive [low, high] for one captured placeholder.

name.description: Unique in the package; the bundle's mapping rows, findings and a rename entry name the rule by it.

match.description: The production names this data rule decides; the compiler matches it. Absent on the management rule.

ranges.description: Per captured placeholder, the values the platform has; the compiler omits a name outside them (omission out_of_range).

node_name.description: What the node's OS calls the port, from captured values, when it differs from the production name; the compiler records it per mapping row for verify's {node_name}. On the management rule, a literal.

management.description: Marks the one rule the compiler applies to the mgmt_only interface.

ref.description: The image reference every measured value here was taken on; the driver's plan writes it into the rendered topology.

pull_secret.description: Present for a gated image (cEOS): the credential provider's name for the registry pull secret clabernetes attaches; the local driver then requires the image present and never pulls it. Absent: a public image either driver may pull.

rule.description: The data rule (interfaces.rules[].name) this rename applies to; the plan looks it up by the mapping row's rule.

port.description: The kind's endpoint name from the rule's captured values; the driver's plan renders it, and counts a rename that drops a placeholder as lossy and two names on one port as shared.

kind.description: The containerlab kind; the plan of both containerlab drivers writes it into the topology.

image.description: The node image and how it is acquired; read by the plan and by the local driver's presence check.

cpu.description: CPUs one node needs; clabernetes sets it as the pod's request, the local driver counts it against its admission budget.

memory_mb.description: Measured memory one node holds, with margin; clabernetes sets it as the pod's request, the local driver counts it against its admission budget. clabernetes 0.10.1 otherwise requests 512 Mi per node, a third of a node's use (measured 2026-10-30).

resources.description: Per node; the plan sums them into the deployment's demand.

deploy_timeout_s.description: Measured bound on bringing this kind's nodes up, an image pull included; the apply phase fails with apply.timeout after it.

destroy_timeout_s.description: Measured bound on removing this kind's nodes; the destroy phase records destroy.timeout and leaves the twin unclean after it.

alias.description: true when the kind accepts production interface names as endpoint aliases, so the plan emits them unchanged; false when it needs rename. Verified 2026-10-30: nokia_srlinux true (ethernet-L/P[/C] accepted, out-of-range names refused in post-deploy); ceos false in containerlab 0.79-0.82, whose pattern eth[1-9][\w.]*$|et[1-9][\w.]*$ is unanchored at the start, so a wrong name ending in et<digit> ("Ethernet1") is accepted and wires a port EOS never sees: the plan emits only rename output for such a kind, and conformance checks every link's port appears in the NOS.

rename.description: For a kind with no aliases, one endpoint template per data rule; the plan renders each production name through it. Absent when alias is true.

link_apply_mode.description: The containerlab link-apply-mode both containerlab drivers write on every node of this kind at create (containerlab 0.79 and clabernetes 0.10.1 both take it; verified on containerlab 0.79 and clabernetes 0.10.1, 2026-10-30). Never changed on a running twin: on clabernetes a changed mode alters the pod spec of each node of this kind and replaces those pods, losing their pushes, and keeps the other device nodes' pods (verified on k3s v1.37.1+k3s1 with clabernetes 0.10.1, 2026-11-05), and a probe host's too [unverified: a probe host's pod under a device's mode change was not read]. live: a link added or removed on a port the node had at boot re-cables with no restart and the push kept, for SR Linux and for cEOS 4.32 alike. restart: the node's pod or container is restarted and re-pushed.

hot_add_ports.description: Whether a port the node did not have at boot appears in the NOS when a link to it is added live. cEOS 4.32: false (verified on containerlab 0.79 and clabernetes 0.10.1, 2026-10-30: the Linux port comes up, EOS never lists it, and a push naming it is accepted silently), so a step that adds such a port must replace the node and re-push, which needs allow_restart. SR Linux 24.7.1: true [unverified: adding a node on a new port of an existing node was measured without checking the existing node's view of that port].

containerlab.description: Read by both containerlab drivers (local and clabernetes).
